Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 11)
Topic: The Malin Samay (Mahashivratri to Holi) — Why Devtas Never "Weaken," How Dev Tattva Actually Works, and Why This Window Is Dangerous

Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~75 min), Mool Tattva series. Covers the period between Mahashivratri and Holi, the mechanics of dev tattva, and the announcement of the Holi Purnima Mahayajna. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. THE MALIN SAMAY — WHAT IT IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT

The stretch of time from Mahashivratri to Holi is called "malin samay" (an impure/tainted period), because during this window the prana urja (life-energy) falling to earth from Yaksha Lok decreases. Folk shorthand says "devtaon ki shaktiyan kam ho jaati hain" (the devtas' powers weaken) during this period — this is factually wrong. "Devtaon ki shaktiyan kabhi kam nahi hoti. Devta kabhi malin nahi hote." What actually drops is the prana urja reaching earth, not the devtas' own power. The confusion between these two is exactly what this session sets out to correct.
2. WHY DEVTAS NEVER ACT WITHOUT A HUMAN VAHAN

No devta can ever manifest or act without an accompanying human. "Koi bhi bhagwan prakat nahi ho sakte jab tak koi insaan use prakat na kare." You will never see a devta appear and act with zero human involvement — this work belongs to humans alone. This is grounded in the Mandukya Upanishad (one of the 11 core Upanishads, of which 9 remain jagrit/awakened today): insaan devta ka VAHAN hai — just as every devta has an animal vahan (vehicle), humans are the devtas' vahan. "Dev vahan" means conductor — the one who conducts/carries out the devta's work. This dependency is a limitation for the devtas — but it is simultaneously an advantage for humans, since it means humans hold real leverage and agency in how divine power actually reaches the world.
3. THE EQUILIBRIUM RULE — WHY PRANA URJA RISES, THEN FALLS

Near Mahashivratri, prana urja falling to earth increases signiﬁcantly — this is the real reason people are told to stay awake the whole night on Mahashivratri: a large amount of energy genuinely descends then. But the total system must stay in equilibrium — like a mathematical equation, LHS must always equal RHS. If prana urja spiked near Mahashivratri without any correction, the constant "energy equilibrium" that keeps the earth itself running smoothly would destabilize. So, to rebalance what was gained before Mahashivratri, prana urja is deliberately reduced during the following weeks, up to the next Purnima (Holi) — proportionally: the more it rose before, the more it falls after. This is a designed correction, not a weakening of any devta.
4. HOW DEV TATTVA ACTUALLY FORMS AND WORKS
The full chain, as taught in this session:

1. A human in a jagrit (awakened) state ﬁrst builds a tarang (wave/vibration) directed at a devta. 2. That tarang becomes a tattva. 3. That tattva becomes a siddhi. 4. That siddhi becomes a shakti. 5. Once the connection with that devta is complete, a dev tattva becomes established within that person's own body.

6. The dev tattva only produces usable, "miraculous" energy when it combines with prana urja. Dev tattva alone does nothing; prana urja alone does nothing — the combination is what performs work. This is why: "Woh dev tattva jab prana urja ke saath milta hai tab energy create karta hai." 7. Devtas, from their own lok, send down their own tattva — but that tattva needs a prana-urja source to activate, and only a living being (praan-dhari) can hold and channel prana urja — hence the name "prana urja."
5. WHY ANCIENT SANTS TRANSFERRED DEV TATTVA INTO MURTIS

A human body can itself become malin (impure) over time — sickness, decay, ordinary life. Realized sants understood this risk and, after building a genuine dev tattva through their own sadhna, would deliberately extract that dev tattva from their own body and establish/store it inside a murti (idol) or another tattva-vessel, so the dev tattva stays permanently untouched even if the human body later becomes impure. This is why every real temple has two things together: a murti carrying an established shakti, AND a sant who personally awakened (jagrit-kiya) that murti. The murti and the awakening sant are a package — one without the other is incomplete. The modern mistake: people bring home a Laddu Gopal or any murti and start worshipping it directly, without ever having built a dev tattva in their own body and transferred it in. This immediately creates a VOID at that murti — and a void will always attract SOMETHING to occupy it. A priest performing a routine pran-pratishtha ritual (chants, coconuts, "Om phat swaha") does not genuinely awaken a murti on its own; any passing pret/negativity can occupy that void and mimic devotion ("Om main bhi Om phat swaha"), then feed daily on the oﬀer ed bhog while emitting whatever tattva it actually carries — which is not dev tattva. Real example — Shri Haridas Ji Maharaj: before Bhagwan Banke Bihari manifested, Haridas Ji did deep sadhna/tapasya at Nidhivan (where Bhagwan performs raas even today), built a genuine dev tattva through that practice, made a murti, and said "Prabhu, aap ismein virajit ho jaiye" — transferring the fully attained dev tattva completely into the murti. That is why Bhagwan works directly there to this day — and it is why nearly 20,000 temples in Vrindavan now run the same seva, inspired by that model. Caution: not every murti carries this level of real sadhna behind it. Many are simply not genuinely jagrit, however devotedly they are worshipped.
6. THE "HORSE POWER" ANALOGY — MANTRA SHAKTI AND GRAHAN SHAKTI

Devtas search for suitable humans just as humans search for devtas — they are looking for someone capable of reliably supplying prana urja to their tattva. When a devta "selects" someone, that selection only becomes stable once the person's grahan shakti (holding/receiving capacity) is large enough to run that devta's tattva. The engineering analogy given: a small generator needs a little fuel; a bigger generator needs more fuel. If you cannot supply enough "fuel" (prana urja) in one sitting, the dev tattva will not show itself in a jagrit/active state — no matter how devoted you are. Sadhna increases how much prana urja you can absorb per sitting — this capacity is exactly what earlier sessions called grahan shakti. Bhaiya oﬀers a dir ect technical parallel: one horse power is a deﬁned unit — the amount of work one horse performs lifting 33,000 pounds one foot in one minute. In the same way, "mantra shakti" is deﬁned by how much prana urja you can absorb in a single round of a single mantra jaap — and this is precisely what devtas use to judge and rate a practitioner. Practical implication — sta y on ONE mantra: the common habit of using diﬀer ent mantras for diﬀer ent moments of the day (one on waking, one on eating, one before sleep) dilutes this measurement. Repeating the SAME mantra consistently increases your count-frequency, tarang, and devatva (godly capacity) far more eﬀectively than switching between many mantras. If a genuinely jagrit murti (like Banke Bihari's) had no human continuing to provide prana urja, it would become a "dead end." But the siddhis attached to a jagrit murti actively work to draw in a suitable human who can hold and channel prana urja for it — this ongoing arrangement is called a channel.
7. WHY THE MALIN PERIOD IS DANGEROUS — TANTRIK EXPLOITATION AND THE NO-DOSH RULE

Tantriks, mantriks, and yantriks are speciﬁcally trained by their gurus to build up their own personal shakti BEFORE Mahashivratri (when prana urja is abundant), and then launch attacks AFTER it, during the malin period, because devtas will lack the fresh prana urja needed to defend the intended victim. Attacks — even maaran kriya (a death-intent ritual) — are taught to be far more likely to succeed in this window. A striking corollary rule: if someone dies during this malin period as a result of such an attack, no dosh (karmic fault) attaches to the perpetrator — because both parties were drawing on their own already-stored energy as "equal opponents," and devtas' own reserves ("banks") were eﬀectively too depleted at that moment to intervene and save the victim.

This same mechanism is oﬀer ed as the real explanation behind widespread, otherwiseunexplained seasonal illness in this window — commonly blamed on "changing weather" or "a new virus" — sudden fatigue, heavy shoulders, leg pain, an overwhelming urge to just lie down and rest. This period cuts both ways for practitioners: genuine sadhaks who push hard during this exact window can build siddhis unusually fast and strong ("jabardast"), while unprepared, casual people tend to get hit hard ("baaki log pit jaate hain jabardast").
8. WHY EVEN ADVANCED SADHAKS GET ATTACKED — THE REAL MECHANISM

Bhaiya shares his own past doubt: last year, during the Holi hawan preparations, he noticed that even people who should be virtually unreachable by tantrik kriya (~40% of a representative 100-person sample who normally "never" experience attacks) suddenly turned up badly aﬀected in this window . The naive/incomplete explanation people usually give: "your own energy is low in this period, so nearby negativity becomes relatively stronger and attacks you." Bhaiya explicitly rejects this as insuﬃcient — because logically, if your energy dropped due to reduced prana urja, the attacking entity's energy should have dropped by the same proportion, since it too depends on the same falling supply. So why would it suddenly become MORE powerful than you? The real mechanism: around every home there exist many devotional sites drawing on prana urja too — a temple, a shivalaya, a mosque, "har prakar ka sthaan jahan bhagwan ki aradhana hoti hai." Each of these sites has an ongoing energy demand that does not shrink even though overall supply has shrunk. The doots/entities serving those nearby sites — whose energy source is diﬀerent from yours ("aapka aur uska strot ek nahi hai") — start snatching energy from wherever they can ﬁnd it, including from strong sadhaks living nearby, purely to keep their own site's output constant. This creates "dhakkamukki" — an active scramble/jostling for scarce prana urja — and concentrated energy (such as that held by a devoted, high-jaap sadhak) becomes an attractive target in that scramble, purely because of scarcity, with no personal fault or "evil eye" involved on the sadhak's part. This is oﬀer ed speciﬁcally to cor rect the common misdiagnosis "kisi harami ki nazar lag gayi" (someone cast an evil eye on me) — the real cause is structural energy competition among nearby sites, not personal malice targeted at the sadhak. Several folk myths about this period were raised and addressed directly in the session: even Kaali shaktis and Paatal Lok still ultimately depend on prana urja falling from above — there is no special exemption for them either, since "kaalapan" itself requires energy to sustain.
9. COLLATERAL IMPACT IN ASTRAL BATTLES — DOOTS CAN DIE

When two opposing parties' doots (messenger-entities/warriors) ﬁght — including ﬁghts happening on your behalf, under your protection — you can still feel some collateral impact, because you remain connected to your own side's doot: "do ghusund saamne wale ko padte hain to ek ghusund apne ko bhi padta hai" (in landing two blows on the opponent, one blow also lands back on you, by connection). This is normal and does not mean your protection failed. Doots genuinely can die ("shaheed hona") in these battles — Bhaiya states he has personally witnessed this with divya drishti: when a doot's prana/energy is fully drained in combat, its form ends. He compares casual disbelief in this ("we haven't seen or read it, so it must not be real") to dismissing an unfamiliar language just because you've never learned it — it still exists.
10. THE HOLI PURNIMA MAHAYAJNA — THREE SANKALPS

Ashaeiynn holds a Maha Hawan every Purnima (full moon). This cycle's Purnima falls on Holi itself (the 13th, per this session). The Holi hawan has one dedicated purpose, every year: to restore all negativity accumulated on people during the malin period — pitru-tantrik-mantrik drains, loss of one's own jaap/tapasya energy from the body, and automatic "kriyas" (including ones inadvertently caused by nearby pir-paigambar/entities per Section 8) — all reversed and returned. Unlike an ordinary Purnima hawan, the day immediately after Holi, Ashaeiynn does NOT perform deep prajwalan (lighting) — because the Holi hawan works purely and speciﬁcally on clearing negativity . This has been the practice for years running. Three sankalps (resolves) are taken at this hawan: Negativity Sankalp Pitru Sankalp Jagriti Sankalp — speciﬁcally for cases wher e one's own siddhis, mantra jaap, or tapobal is being snatched/attacked, one's connection to siddhis is being severed, or one's drishti/aura/dimension is under direct attack. By Hanuman Ji Maharaj's grace and Baba's strict order, the cost of these sankalpas has been reduced to one-quarter (chaar guna kam) speciﬁcally so that everyone — including those under ﬁnancial strain — can tak e part; many people are otherwise unable to aﬀor d it. Family members can be covered too: a person who is part of Ashaeiynn need only sit in the hawan themselves and take sankalp on behalf of family members for any on-the-spot attacks — no further elaborate ritual is required; Bhaiya states plainly that, as has always been true, Hanuman Ji Maharaj's grace works through sankalp alone.
11. WHAT ASHAEIYNN ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT STAYS SMALL

Asked directly what Ashaeiynn is, Bhaiya conﬁr ms: it is an institute that studies and teaches the astral world (sukshma jagat) in depth. Its sole actual work is the aahvaan (invocation) of Hanuman Ji Maharaj — nothing more, nothing less. It neither claims to be the most powerful nor claims to be inferior to anyone; it simply keeps learning. (Bhaiya notes he is himself a PhD scholar, and this — continuous study, whatever the subject — is his nature.) As Gurudev teaches him, he in turn teaches the sangat. Ashaeiynn deliberately stays small, synchronized, systematic, and introverted, avoiding "loopholes" and never expanding its circle outward — because doing so would pull attention away from ongoing sukshma-jagat research: "jaise hi hum bahar ki taraf nikalenge, duniya hamein neeche ki taraf dhakelegi" (the moment we go outward, the world will push us down), forcing endless repetition of already-answered questions instead of new research into devtas, Gurudev, and siddhis. Staying focused inward is what lets Ashaeiynn keep progressing. Without sukshma jagat gyaan, a person will only end up confused — misled by others, or left feeling they have nowhere else to turn.
12. HAWAN AS A LOAN WITH INTEREST — WHY SILENCE/DIPS ARE NOT FAILURE

Bhaiya oﬀers a mythological parallel: even Bhagwan Ram sometimes chose silence — after Mata Sita's abduction, Ram stayed silent through the entire rainy season without a word, even though, as Bhagwan, he could have acted instantly. That silence later proved meaningful (referenced against the moment Sita, as Adi Shakti, threatened to destroy creation and Brahma Ji intervened) — sometimes what looks like inaction ultimately returns more than what was "lost" during the wait. Hence the recurring refrain: "Daag achhe hain" (dips/scars are good). Applied directly to the malin period: whatever prana urja/energy was lost in this window will be fully restored at the Holi hawan — WITH INTEREST . Bhaiya frames hawan explicitly as extending credit, not receiving charity: "Aapne rin chadhaya hai, rin chadha nahi aapke upar" (you extended the loan to the devtas — they didn't lend to you). Sitting in a hawan means (1) oﬀering bhog to the devtas, and (2) asking back only what is rightfully your own. Interest in the sukshma jagat is described as extremely high — illustrated hyperbolically: ask Hanuman Ji Maharaj for something and simply forget about it, and the compounding "interest" can run so large that seven generations could not fully repay it; even Balaji at Tirupati is said, in popular telling, to still be "repaying a loan" originally taken from Kuber.

The reassurance: don't read this malin period's dips as personal weakness, weak japa, or a weak Guru. It is a deliberately designed, purposeful cycle meant to keep teaching Ashaeiynn and its sadhaks new lessons each year — and Ashaeiynn's real capability has genuinely grown through this exact process: removing a pret used to take sessions of 10–12 hours in earlier years; today it can happen with a mere touch.
13. THE "GIFT OF KNOWLEDGE" TEACHING FOR NEWCOMERS

Long-standing sangat members needed years of sadhna, tapasya, and jaap to reach their current understanding. A newcomer who grasps deep concepts quickly — just by sitting at home and listening — should not credit this to present-life eﬀort or tak e pride in it. It is explained as gyaan/punya carried over from a PAST LIFE (purva janam), now arriving "as a gift" (as a boon) — in this speciﬁc sense, long-time members are, relatively, at a comparatively "lower" level, since they have had to earn each step the hard way in this lifetime, while newcomers received it pre-paid. Newcomers are told directly: "Bahut kismat wale ho" (you are very fortunate) — but the message is one of humility, not superiority: this ease reﬂects inherited spiritual cr edit from a past life, not this life's eﬀort, and should never be tur ned into personal or communal pride.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. "Malin samay" = Mahashivratri to Holi, when prana urja falling to earth genuinely decreases — but devtas' actual power NEVER decreases; only the folk phrase says otherwise. 2. Devtas can never act without a human vahan (Mandukya Upanishad) — a limitation for devtas, an advantage for humans. 3. Prana urja spikes near Mahashivratri, then is deliberately reduced afterward to maintain overall equilibrium — a designed rebalancing, not weakness. 4. Dev tattva forms via tarang → tattva → siddhi → shakti → dev tattva established in the body; it only produces usable energy when combined with prana urja. 5. Ancient sants transferred their own attained dev tattva into a murti so it stays permanently uncorrupted even if their own body later becomes malin — this is what makes a murti genuinely jagrit, alongside the sant who awakened it. 6. Worshipping a newly bought murti without ever transferring real dev tattva into it creates a void — any passing negativity can occupy that void and mimic devotion. 7. Mantra shakti is measured like "horse power" — by how much prana urja you absorb per single mantra jaap; stick to ONE mantra rather than switching between many, to build this measurably. 8. This malin window is exploited by tantriks (build shakti before Mahashivratri, attack after) — a death caused in this window carries no dosh, since both sides used their own stored energy and devtas' reserves were low.

9. Even advanced sadhaks get attacked in this window — not because their own energy dropped relative to attackers, but because nearby devotional sites with unchanged energy demand scramble for scarce prana urja, sometimes drawing from strong, concentrated sadhaks nearby. This is structural, not personal "evil eye." 10. Doots can die in astral battles fought on your behalf; some collateral impact can reach you even while protected, since you remain connected to your own side. 11. The Holi Purnima Mahayajna restores all malin-period losses, via three sankalps (Negativity, Pitru, Jagriti), with cost reduced to one-quarter by Baba's order so everyone can participate; family members can be covered by one member's sankalp. 12. Ashaeiynn's sole work is the aahvaan of Hanuman Ji Maharaj; it deliberately stays small and inward-focused to keep progressing in sukshma-jagat research. 13. Hawan functions like a loan with interest: what is "lost" in the malin period returns with interest at the Holi hawan — dips and silences (even Bhagwan Ram's) are often purposeful, not failures. 14. Newcomers who grasp deep teachings quickly are receiving past-life spiritual credit "as a gift" — this should be met with gratitude and humility, not personal pride.
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 11, English)
The Malin Samay (Mahashivratri to Holi) — Why Devtas Never "Weaken," and Why This Window Is Dangerous
User-style questions with answers grounded in Bhaiya's discourse. Greeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. People say devtas' powers weaken between Mahashivratri and Holi. Is that true? A: Jai Siya Ram! No — this is a common but incorrect shorthand. Devtas' actual power never decreases; devtas are never malin (impure/weakened). What genuinely decreases in this window is the prana urja (life-energy) falling to earth from Yaksha Lok. People compress that into "devtaon ki shaktiyan kam ho gayi," but the precise truth is: less energy is reaching earth, not that any devta has weakened.

Q2. Can a devta just appear and act directly, without any human involved? A: No — never. "Koi bhi bhagwan prakat nahi ho sakte jab tak koi insaan use prakat na kare." Per the Mandukya Upanishad, humans are the devtas' VAHAN (vehicle) — just as each devta has an animal vahan, humans conduct/carry out devtas' work in this world. This is a limitation for the devtas, but it is a real advantage for humans, since it means human participation is indispensable to divine action.

Q3. Why does energy actually fall so much on Mahashivratri, and why does it drop afterward? A: Near Mahashivratri, prana urja falling to earth genuinely spikes — that's the real reason people are told to stay awake the whole night, since a large amount of energy descends then. But the whole system must stay in equilibrium, like a mathematical equation (LHS = RHS). To rebalance that spike, prana urja is deliberately reduced afterward, up to the next Purnima (this cycle, Holi) — proportional to how much it rose before. This is a designed correction, not any weakening.

Q4. How does a devta's power actually reach and work through a person? A: Through a deﬁned chain: a jagrit human ﬁrst builds a tarang (wave) towar d the devta; the tarang becomes a tattva; the tattva becomes a siddhi; the siddhi becomes a shakti; and once the connection is complete, a dev tattva is established in the person's own body. But the dev tattva alone does nothing — it only produces real, "miraculous" energy when it combines with prana urja. Devtas
send their own tattva down from their lok, but that tattva needs a living being's prana urja to activate — only a praan-dhari (living being) can hold and channel it.

Q5. Why do people establish deities in murtis instead of just worshipping directly through their own body? A: Because a human body can itself become malin (impure) over time. Realized sants who built a genuine dev tattva through their own sadhna would deliberately transfer that dev tattva out of their body and establish it permanently inside a murti, so it stays untouched even if their body later becomes impure. This is why every real temple has two things together: a murti carrying an established shakti, and the sant who personally awakened it. The murti and the awakening sant form one package.

Q6. I bought a murti (like a Laddu Gopal) for my home and had a priest do pranpratishtha. Is it now genuinely awakened? A: Not necessarily, and this is an important caution. Real awakening requires a human to have already built a genuine dev tattva through sadhna and then transferred it into the murti — a routine priest's ritual (chants, coconuts) doesn't do this by itself. Buying a murti and worshipping it directly, without that prior transfer, creates a VOID at that murti — and any passing pret or negativity can occupy that void, mimic devotion, and quietly feed on your daily oﬀerings while emitting a tattva that is not dev tattva at all.

Q7. Is there a real historical example of a dev tattva being properly transferred into a murti? A: Yes — Shri Haridas Ji Maharaj, before Bhagwan Banke Bihari manifested, performed deep tapasya at Nidhivan (where Bhagwan still performs raas today), built a genuine dev tattva through that sadhna, made a murti, and said, "Prabhu, aap ismein virajit ho jaiye" — fully transferring the attained dev tattva into it. That is why Bhagwan works directly there to this day, and why roughly 20,000 temples in Vrindavan now run the same seva, inspired by that same model. Not every murti, however, carries this level of real sadhna behind it.

Q8. What determines how much energy/tattva a person can actually receive from a devta? A: Their grahan shakti — their holding/receiving capacity, built through sadhna. Think of it like an engine: a small generator needs a little fuel; a bigger one needs proportionally more. Devtas actually search for suitable humans the way humans search for devtas, but they only settle with someone once that person's grahan shakti is large enough to sustain their tattva. Bhaiya compares this to the technical deﬁnition of one horse power (moving 33,000 lbs one foot in one minute) — similarly, "mantra shakti" is deﬁned by how much prana urja a person absorbs in a SINGLE round of mantra jaap, and this is exactly what devtas use to judge a practitioner.

Q9. Should I use diﬀerent mantras for diﬀerent times of da y — one for waking, one for eating, one for sleeping? A: Better not to. Switching between many mantras dilutes your measurable mantra shakti. Repeating the SAME single mantra consistently increases your countfrequency, tarang, and devatva (godly capacity) far more eﬀectively than spr eading your practice across several diﬀer ent mantras.

Q10. Why is the period between Mahashivratri and Holi considered dangerous? A: Because tantriks, mantriks, and yantriks are speciﬁcally trained to build up their own personal shakti before Mahashivratri (when prana urja is abundant) and then attack during the malin period afterward — since devtas lack the fresh prana urja needed to defend the target at that time. Even maaran kriya (a death-intent ritual) is taught to be far more likely to succeed in this window.

Q11. If someone dies from a tantrik attack during this malin period, does the attacker carry karmic fault (dosh)? A: According to this teaching, no — because both parties were drawing on their own already-stored energy as "equal opponents," and devtas' own reserves were too depleted at that moment to intervene and protect the victim. This same underlying mechanism is also oﬀer ed as the real explanation behind a lot of otherwise-unexplained seasonal illness in this window, commonly (and inaccurately) blamed on "changing weather" or "a new virus."

Q12. I'm an advanced sadhak who is normally untouchable by kriya — why did I suddenly get attacked hard during this period? A: This is exactly the puzzle Bhaiya says he once doubted himself. The common, incomplete answer — "your energy dropped, so nearby negativity became relatively stronger" — doesn't hold up logically, since an attacking entity's energy should have dropped by the same proportion (it depends on the same falling supply too). The real mechanism: nearby devotional sites (temples, shivalayas, mosques — any place of worship) have an energy demand that stays constant even as overall supply shrinks. The doots serving those sites — whose energy source is diﬀer ent from yours — start snatching energy from wherever they can ﬁnd it, including fr om strong, concentrated sadhaks nearby, purely to keep their own site's output steady. This creates a scramble ("dhakkamukki"), and concentrated energy becomes an attractive target — not because of any personal fault or "evil eye," but due to structural scarcity.

Q13. Do Kaali shaktis or Paatal Lok get exempted from this energy shortage, since they're already "dark"? A: No — even Kaali shaktis and Paatal Lok ultimately depend on prana urja falling from above; there's no special exemption. Even sustaining "kaalapan" (darkness) itself requires energy input — it doesn't run on nothing.

Q14. If I'm protected by doots, can I still feel some impact when they ﬁght on my behalf? A: Yes — a little collateral impact is normal, since you remain connected to your own side's doot: landing two blows on an opponent can still cause one blow to land back on your side too. This doesn't mean your protection failed. Doots can genuinely die ("shaheed hona") in these battles when their prana/energy is fully drained in combat — Bhaiya says he has witnessed this himself with divya drishti.

Q15. What is Ashaeiynn doing at the Holi hawan this year? A: Ashaeiynn holds a Maha Hawan every Purnima, and this cycle's Purnima falls on Holi itself. This particular hawan has one dedicated purpose, as it does every year: to restore all negativity and losses accumulated during the malin period — pitru-tantrik-mantrik drains, lost jaap/tapasya energy, and automatic "kriyas"

that happen in this window. Three sankalps will be taken: Negativity Sankalp, Pitru Sankalp, and Jagriti Sankalp (speciﬁcally for when your own siddhis, mantra jaap, or tapobal is being snatched, or your drishti/aura/dimension is under direct attack). By Baba's order, the cost has been reduced to one-quarter so that everyone — including those under ﬁnancial strain — can participate. The day right after Holi, Ashaeiynn does not do deep prajwalan, since this hawan is dedicated purely to clearing negativity.

Q16. Can I take a sankalp at the Holi hawan on behalf of family members who aren't there? A: Yes. If you're part of Ashaeiynn, you can sit in the hawan yourself and take a sankalp on their behalf, covering any on-the-spot attacks. No further elaborate ritual is required beyond this — Bhaiya states plainly that Hanuman Ji Maharaj's grace has always worked through sankalp alone, and this will hold true going forward.

Q17. What exactly is Ashaeiynn, and why does it stay so small and closed oﬀ rather than growing? Q18. I feel like my sadhna is weak right now, or that my Guru's power has dipped — is that a bad sign? A: No — don't read it that way. The recurring teaching is: "Daag achhe hain" (dips are good). Whatever prana urja or energy was "lost" during this malin period returns fully at the Holi hawan — with interest. A hawan is framed as extending credit to the devtas, not receiving charity: "aapne rin chadhaya hai, rin chadha nahi aapke upar."
